bubbles ascending in a shear thinning liquid rise faster and straighter compared to Newtonian liquids and the bubble rising behaviour is influenced by the bubble size, liquid velocity and channel depth.
the rising behaviour of a bubble in a confined geometry is significantly influenced by the rheology of a continuous phase, the channel depth, bubble size and superimposed liquid flow velocity.

the rheological properties of the continuous phase, the channel depth, the bubble size and the superimposed liquid flow rate are the most important parameters influencing the bubble behaviour in confined geometries.

the rising behaviour of single bubbles and the resulting mass transfer in narrow rectangular channels.
the rising behaviour of single bubbles and the effect of the rheology and geometry of the liquid in which the bubbles are rising.
the rising behaviour of single bubbles ascending through rectangular channels with a spacing of 5 to 7 mm in Newtonian and in shear thinning liquids.

the rising behaviour of single bubbles is influenced by all the parameters investigated in this study.
the rising bubble behaviour in the shear thin ning liquid is more stable and more predictable than in Newtonian liquid.

a bubble rising in a confined rectangular channel with a shear thinning liquid is characterized by a more straight rising path and less oscillations.
